title: Latin Building Blocks
kidRule: Many English words are built from little Latin pieces. AQUA means water, PORT means carry, STRUCT means build, RUPT means break, AUD means hear, SPECT means look, and DICT means say. Find the piece and you have found the tricky part: TRANS + PORT = TRANSPORT.
hint: A Latin piece is hiding in this word. Can you hear AQUA, PORT, STRUCT, RUPT, AUD, SPECT or DICT? Spell that piece the way it is always spelled.
reminder: Spell the Latin piece the same way every time: A-Q-U-A, P-O-R-T, S-T-R-U-C-T, R-U-P-T, A-U-D, S-P-E-C-T, D-I-C-T. The 'kt' sound at the end is always C-T.

check.question: Why does PREDICT end with the letters D-I-C-T?
check.correctAnswer: It is built from the Latin piece DICT, which means say: you say what will happen before it does!
distractors: Because every word about the future ends with C-T
Because the letter K is never allowed near the end of a word

words.def: To carry people or things from one place to another.
words.sent: Big trucks transport apples from the farm to the store.
words.story: Trans means across and port means carry, so to transport something is to carry it across!
words.card: It is a silly *sport* to *transport* a hippo on a skateboard!

words.def: To say what you think will happen before it happens.
words.sent: I predict that it will snow tonight.
words.story: Pre means before and dict means say, so to predict is to 'say before'. Weather scientists predict storms days ahead by studying the clouds and the wind!
words.card: I *predict* my face will turn *red* when I eat the spicy pepper!

words.def: To build something by putting parts together.
words.sent: Beavers construct dams out of sticks and mud.
words.story: Beavers construct dams from sticks and mud. The longest one ever found, in Canada, is about 850 meters long!
words.card: The squirrels will *construct* a castle out of pine *con*es!

words.def: To look at something very carefully.
words.sent: The vet will inspect the puppy's teeth.
words.story: In means into and spect means look, so to inspect is to 'look into'. Before every flight, a pilot walks all the way around the airplane to inspect it!
words.card: The wood*pec*ker stopped to *inspect* every single tree for snacks!

words.def: To stop someone in the middle of talking or doing something.
words.sent: Please do not interrupt while the teacher is reading.
words.story: Inter means between and rupt means break, so when you interrupt you 'break in between'. That is why there are two Rs: one from each piece!
words.card: Do not *interrupt* the p*up*py when it is telling a joke!

words.sent: The mouse's squeak was barely audible.
words.story: Aud means hear. Elephants make rumbles so low that they are not audible to people, but other elephants can hear them from far away!
words.card: The terr*ible* burp was *audible* all the way to the moon!

words.def: To burst out suddenly, the way melted rock bursts out of a volcano.
words.sent: Scientists can often tell when a volcano is about to erupt.
words.story: The E means out and rupt means break, so to erupt is to 'break out'. Kilauea in Hawaii is one of the most active volcanoes on Earth!
words.card: Squeeze too hard and the sy*rup* will *erupt* all over the pancakes!

words.def: A person who watches a game or a show.
words.sent: Every spectator cheered when the runner crossed the line.
words.story: Spect means look, so a spectator is a looker. The same piece hides in spectacles, which are glasses for looking!
words.card: One *spectator* was so tiny he was just a *spec*k in the top row!

words.sent: A water lily is an aquatic plant.
words.story: Aqua means water. Sea otters are aquatic animals, and they sometimes hold paws while they sleep so they do not drift apart!
words.card: The *aquatic* frog has a very *tic*klish tummy!

words.def: A big room with rows of seats where people watch and listen to a show.
words.sent: The whole school sat in the auditorium for the concert.
words.story: Aud means hear, and in Latin an auditorium was simply 'a place for hearing'!
words.card: Y*um*! Someone is crunching popcorn in the quiet *auditorium*!
